Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 41, verses 1–2:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surat Fussilat

(Ha Mim, as-Sajda) It is named so because it contains the verse of prostration. It indicates the nullity of worshipping manifestations (al-mazahir) absolutely, and that Allah, by His very essence, deserves the most exalted forms of worship. This is among the greatest aims of the Qur'an. So said al-Mahayimi. It is a Meccan surah, and its verses number fifty-four.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Discourse on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[1, 2] ﴿Ha Mim﴾ ﴿A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾ [Fussilat: 2].

﴿Ha Mim﴾ ﴿A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾ [Fussilat: 2]. Abu as-Su'ud said: If "Ha Mim" is taken as the name of the surah, then it is either the predicate of an omitted subject (mubtada' mahdhuf), which is the more apparent view, or a subject whose predicate is: "A revelation" (tanzil). In the first case, it is a predicate following a predicate, and a predicate for an omitted subject, if it is taken as a sequence in the manner of enumeration. And His words, exalted is He: ﴿from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾ [Fussilat: 2] are connected to it, emphasizing what the tanwin conveys of inherent majesty with additional majesty through the genitive construction. Or it is another predicate. Or: "A revelation" (tanzil) is a subject, being specified by its qualifier, whose predicate is: ﴿a Book whose verses have been detailed﴾ [Fussilat: 3].

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[3] ﴿A Book whose verses have been detailed, an Arabic Qur'an for a people who know.﴾

﴿A Book﴾: According to the earlier possibilities, it is a substitute (badal) for the preceding word, or a separate predicate (khabar), or the predicate of an omitted subject. The attribution of the revelation to the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, serves to announce that it is the source of religious and worldly benefits, occurring in accordance with the requirement of Lordly mercy, as His saying indicates: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾ [al-Anbiya' 107]. ﴿Whose verses have been detailed﴾: that is, made clear by comprising all religious matters together with rational proofs. ﴿An Arabic Qur'an﴾: that is, in the Arabic tongue, in which there is facilitated, from all benefits, what is not facilitated in other than it. The accusative of ﴿Qur'anan﴾ is either by way of praise, or as a circumstantial clause (hal) from ﴿Book﴾ because it is specified by its qualifier, or from ﴿its verses﴾. ﴿For a people who know﴾: that is, its measure and its meanings, or for the people of knowledge and reflection.

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[4] ﴿A bringer of good tidings and a warner, but most of them turned away, so they do not hear.﴾

﴿A bringer of good tidings﴾ means: to those who act upon it, reflect upon it, and derive from it, with everlasting bliss. ﴿And a warner﴾ means: to those who turn away from it, with eternal abiding in the Fire of Hell. ﴿But most of them turned away﴾ means: most of these people, to whom this Qur'an was sent down as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, did not contemplate it. ﴿So they do not hear﴾ means: they do not lend it an ear, out of arrogance and haughtiness.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[5] ﴿And they say: "Our hearts are in coverings (akinna) against that to which you call us, and in our ears is a deafness, and between us and you there is a barrier. So act, for we are acting."﴾

﴿And they say: "Our hearts are in coverings against that to which you call us"﴾ i.e., in thick veils, so that nothing of what you call us to reaches them, of monotheism (tawhid) and of confirming what is in this Qur'an of commands, prohibitions, promises and threats. ﴿And in our ears is a deafness﴾ i.e., a deafness (waqr), so that we do not hear that, out of distaste for it and aversion to it. ﴿And between us and you there is a barrier﴾ i.e., there is no connection and no meeting on that to which we are called. ﴿So act﴾ i.e., act according to what you call to, and strive for it. ﴿For we are acting﴾ i.e., according to what we found our fathers upon.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 41, verses 6–8:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[6–8] ﴿Say, "I am but a human being like you. It has been revealed to me that your God is but one God, so take the straight course to Him and seek His forgiveness." And woe to those who associate others with Allah ﴿who do not give zakah and who are, in the Hereafter, disbelievers﴾ [Fussilat: 7] ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds will have a reward uninterrupted﴾ [Fussilat: 8].

(p-5188) ﴿Say, "I am but a human being like you. It has been revealed to me that your God is but one God, so take the straight course to Him"﴾ That is, through monotheism (tawhid) and sincerity in worship, without deviating into falsehood and the scattered paths.

﴿And seek His forgiveness﴾ That is, by repenting from shirk. ﴿And woe to those who associate others with Allah﴾ ﴿who do not give zakah﴾ [Fussilat: 7] That is, they do not purify their souls through obedience to Allah, or they do not spend the zakah from their wealth. This is what Ibn Jarir preferred, on the view that this is the most well-known meaning of zakah, especially given the accompanying use of "giving" (iitaa').

In this there is an indication that among the most distinctive attributes of the disbelievers is withholding zakah, so that the believers may be warned against committing it. And from Qatadah: "Zakah is the bridge of Islam; whoever cuts it off is saved, and whoever falls short of it is destroyed." Ibn Jarir said: The apostates after the Prophet of Allah said, "As for prayer, we will pray. As for zakah, by Allah, our wealth will not be taken from us." So Abu Bakr said, "By Allah, I will not separate between two things that Allah has joined. By Allah, if they withhold from me even a cord (iqal) of what Allah and His Messenger have enjoined, I will fight them over it."

﴿And they, in the Hereafter﴾ [Fussilat: 7] That is, by their being brought back to life after their death for recompense: ﴿they are disbelievers﴾ [Fussilat: 7]

﴿Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds will have a reward uninterrupted﴾ [Fussilat: 8] That is, it is not withheld from them, or not diminished, or not cut off, or not counted.

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:**

[9, 10] ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days, and set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿He placed firmly set mountains upon it from above it, and blessed it, and measured therein its sustenance in four days, equal for those who ask.﴾ [Fussilat: 10].

﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days﴾, meaning: in the measure of the two days, and their knowledge of the relative clause (ṣilat al-mawṣūl). As for what they received, generation after generation, and it spread among them, or what they heard from the earlier books, such as the Torah, their souls submitted to this, until it became familiar to them. ﴿And you set up rivals to Him﴾, meaning: equals (akfā'), ﴿and there is none comparable to Him﴾ [al-Ikhlas: 4]. ﴿That﴾, meaning: He who created the earth in two days, ﴿is the Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿He placed firmly set mountains﴾ [Fussilat: 10], meaning: fixed mountains. ﴿Upon it from above it, and blessed it﴾ [Fussilat: 10], meaning: He multiplied its good. ﴿And measured therein its sustenance in four days, equal for those who ask﴾ [Fussilat: 10], meaning: equal in proportion and balance, for those seeking sustenance and means of living; that is, He measured it for them. Or it means: for one who asks about the length of the term in which God created the earth, placed in it the firm mountains and the blessing, and determined its sustenance. So He defined it, as He informed, exalted is He, and it is four days.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 41, verse 11:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[11] ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: "Come, willingly or unwillingly." They said: "We come willingly."﴾

﴿Then He turned to the heaven﴾ means: He intended to bring them both into existence. As for "thumma" (then), it indicates the difference between the two creations in terms of perfection and its absence, and their difference in direction and substance, not a delay in time, since there is no time there. So said al-Qashani.

Ibn Jarir said: That is, "then He rose up to the heaven," meaning without modality (takyif) and without likening (tamthil). ﴿And it was smoke﴾. Al-Qashani said: That is, a subtle substance, unlike the dense, heavy, earthly substances. Al-Qadi said: "Smoke" is something dark, and perhaps he meant by it its matter, or the minute particles from which it was composed. Its origin is in al-Razi, where he said: When God Most High created the indivisible particles, before He created in them the quality of light, they were dark and devoid of luminosity. Then when He assembled them and made them heavens, stars, a sun and a moon, and brought into them the attribute of light (p-5190), they then became luminous. Thus it is established that those particles, when God Most High intended to create from them the heavens, the sun and the moon, were dark. So naming them "smoke" is correct, because smoke has no meaning except scattered particles, not connected to one another, devoid of light. Then he said: This is what occurred to the mind regarding the interpretation of the smoke. And God knows best the reality of the matter. End of quotation.

Some scholars of astronomy said in explaining this verse: ﴿And it was smoke﴾, that is, particles, that is, gases, that is, a nebula. Then they attracted one another as clouds gather, and became a single mass, in confirmation of His saying: ﴿Have those who disbelieved not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and We separated them﴾ [al-Anbiya': 30], that is, a single mass. Then it revolved and broke apart and separated through the repelling force, and the earth and the heavens were formed, in confirmation of His saying: ﴿And We separated them﴾ [al-Anbiya': 30], that is, We divided them. They became spheres of water in two days, that is, two thousand years, according to His saying: ﴿And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾ [al-Hajj: 47]. At that time His Throne was upon the water, that is, His dominion and authority were over the water, and God knows best. End of quotation. And God knows best.

﴿Then He said to it and to the earth: "Come, willingly or unwillingly." They said: "We come willingly."﴾ Al-Qashani said: That is, His command and will were connected to bringing them both into existence, so they were found at once, together, like the obedient subordinate who, when the command of an obeyed commander arrives, does not delay in carrying it out. This is by way of figurative representation (tamthil), since there is no speech there. End of quotation.

Ibn Jarir said: That is, God, exalted is His praise, said to the heaven and the earth: "Bring forth what I have created in you. As for you, O heaven, make appear what I have created in you of the sun, the moon and the stars. As for you, O earth, bring out what I have created in you of trees, fruits and plants, and split open for the rivers." ﴿They said: "We come willingly"﴾, that is, we bring what You have produced in us of Your creation, responding to Your command, not disobeying Your order. End of quotation.

The meaning is that attributing a dialogue to the heaven and the earth is a metaphor (majaz). It is either by way of the implicit metaphor (al-isti'arah al-makniyyah), as when you say "the situation spoke" (nataqat al-hal), so the situation is treated as a person who speaks in indicating [its meaning], and then speech, which is a necessary attribute of the thing compared to, is imagined for it and attributed to it. Or it is by way of the metaphor of representation (al-isti'arah al-tamthiliyyah), by likening in it the state of the heaven and the earth, which lie between Him and their Creator, in the will to form and bring them into existence, to the state of a mighty ruler whose authority is effective, and whose subjects obey under his disposal without hesitation.

Some have rejected the view of those who held that inanimate things possess discernment and speech according to the outward meaning of such texts, including Ibn Hazm. He said in al-Fisal: As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They said: "We come willingly"﴾, we know by necessity and observation that speech in the language in which the Qur'an was revealed is only the expulsion of the instruments of speech from the pipes of the chest, the throat, the palate, the tongue, the lips and the molars, by air that reaches the ears of the listener, so that he understands the speaker's meanings through it. Since there is no doubt about this, whoever has no tongue, no lips, no molars, no palate and no throat cannot produce the speech known to us. No person of intellect doubts this. Since this is so, as we have said by direct observation, every utterance that is reported in a text about one who does not have this attribute is not the speech known to us, but another meaning. Since this is as we have mentioned, it is by necessity established that the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿We come willingly﴾ is only upon the effectiveness of His judgment, the mighty and majestic, and His disposing of them both. End of quotation.

The same applies to: ﴿Come, willingly or unwillingly﴾. For when they were treated, while they are of the inanimate things, as if they were rational beings, since they were commanded and addressed by way of the implicit or representational metaphor, He attributed to them what is among the attributes of rational beings, namely willingness and unwillingness, as a supporting element (tarshih). They are interpreted as "obedient" and "unwilling," because the verbal noun (masdar) cannot occur as a circumstantial qualifier (hal) without that. It is also permissible that they be an absolute object (maf'ul mutlaq). He said ﴿ta'i'in﴾ (obedient) in the sound masculine plural form, although it is specific to rational male beings. The apparent expectation would have been ﴿ta'i'at﴾ (obedient, feminine plural) or ﴿ta'i'atayn﴾ (obedient, feminine dual), in view of the address, the response, and the description with willingness and unwillingness.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[12] ﴿So He completed them as seven heavens within two days, and inspired in each heaven its command. And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and as a protection. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.﴾

(p-5192) ﴿So He completed them as seven heavens within two days﴾ i.e., He perfected them by removing the softness of the smoke. Al-Mahayimi said: "No day was assigned to their substance, because it is like the substance of the earth; so it entered into its day." ﴿And He inspired in each heaven its command﴾ i.e., what He commanded in it, and what He arranged of the angels and the creation within it, and what is not known. ﴿And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps﴾ for it is like a raised ceiling adorned with lamps suspended from it, which calls one to reflect upon them as evidence of the power and wisdom of their Maker. ﴿And as a protection﴾ i.e., from the devils, lest they steal the news of it. ﴿That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.﴾

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[13] ﴿So if they turn away, say: I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ʿĀd and Thamūd.﴾

﴿So if they turn away﴾, i.e., from this reasoning and from believing in this Mighty, Victorious One over everything, whose knowledge necessitated the ordering of some matters. ﴿Say: I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ʿĀd and Thamūd﴾, because you are like them in obstinacy, like ʿĀd in arrogance, and like Thamūd in preferring blindness over guidance. Ibn Jarīr said: We have already explained earlier that the meaning of ṣāʿiqa (thunderbolt) is whatever destroys a thing and changes it from its state. It was also said regarding this matter: it refers to a calamity from God and a punishment.

al-Qawl fi ta'wil qawlihi Ta'ala:

[14-16] ﴿When the messengers came to them from before them and from behind them, saying: "Worship none but Allah." They said: "If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels. So we disbelieve in what you have been sent with."﴾ ﴿As for 'Ad, they were arrogant in the land without right and said: "Who is mightier than us in strength?" Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is mightier than them in strength? And they used to deny Our signs.﴾ [Fussilat: 15] ﴿So We sent upon them a furious wind during days of misfortune, that We might make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world. But the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing, and they will not be helped.﴾ [Fussilat: 16]

(p-5193) ﴿When the messengers came to them from before them and from behind them﴾. Al-Zamakhshari said: That is, they came to them from every side, exerted themselves with them, and employed every stratagem with them, yet they saw from them nothing but obstinacy and aversion. This is like what Allah, Exalted, related about Satan: ﴿I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them﴾ [al-A'raf: 17], meaning: I will surely come to them from every direction and will surely employ every stratagem against them. One says: "I went around (istdartu) a person from every side, and I had no stratagem regarding him."

Its essential meaning is that the two directions are a metaphor (kinayah) for all directions, as is known in similar usages. What is meant by their coming from all directions is the exertion of effort in calling them, by way of metaphor. It is also possible that the meaning is: they came to them with admonition from the direction of the past time, and what befell the disbelievers in it, and from the direction of the future, and what will befall them. Thus what is meant by "before them" is the past time, and by "behind them" is the future. The reverse is also permissible, as was mentioned in the verse of the Throne (ayat al-Kursi).

﴿Worship none but Allah. They said: If our Lord had willed﴾, that is, to send a messenger, ﴿He would have sent down angels﴾, that is, from the heaven, with what you call us to. ﴿So we disbelieve in what you have been sent with﴾, that is, of worshipping Allah alone. ﴿As for 'Ad, they were arrogant in the land without right and said: "Who is mightier than us in strength?"﴾ [Fussilat: 15], that is, so that we need not fear His punishment if we abandon His worship or worship another along with Him.

﴿Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is mightier than them in strength?﴾ [Fussilat: 15], that is, therefore His punishment must be feared and His chastisement guarded against. ﴿And they used to deny Our signs﴾ [Fussilat: 15], that is, those which are the strongest proofs. ﴿So We sent upon them﴾ [Fussilat: 16], that is, because of their arrogance through strength, ﴿a furious wind﴾ [Fussilat: 16], that is, intensely loud in its blowing, ﴿during days of misfortune﴾ [Fussilat: 16], that is, ill-omened for them, ﴿that We might make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world. But the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing, and they will not be helped﴾ [Fussilat: 16], that is, in the Hereafter, just as they were not helped in this world.

Note: Al-Razi said: The astrologers (al-Ahkamiyyun min al-munajjimin, i.e., those who judge events by the stars) used this verse as evidence that some days may be ill-omened (nahs) and some may be fortunate (sa'd), since ill-omen is opposed by good fortune, and turbidity is opposed by clarity. Then al-Razi extended the discussion of the response and the objection at length. It is not hidden that fortune and misfortune are a relative matter, not an inherent one. Otherwise, the day that the astrologers see as ill-omened would be ill-omened for everything the sun shines upon, and likewise what they see as fortunate would be fortunate for everything; but the reality is otherwise, since a day that is ill-omened for Zayd may be fortunate for Bakr. Indeed, an hour, indeed a minute. So where is that claim? The Qur'an came in the wondrous style of the Arabs, and among their subtleties is calling a time of hardship and distress "ill-omened" (nahs) and its opposite "fortunate" (sa'd). So the ill-omened is ill-omened for its owner, and the fortunate is fortunate for its owner.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 41, verse 17:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[17] ﴿And as for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance, so the thunderbolt of the humiliating punishment seized them for what they used to earn.﴾

﴿And as for Thamud, We guided them﴾ meaning: We made clear to them the path of truth and the way of right guidance, and We forbade them to follow misguidance and commanded them to pursue guidance. ﴿But they preferred blindness over guidance, so the thunderbolt of the humiliating punishment seized them for what they used to earn﴾ meaning: of sins, through their disbelief in Allah.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[18] ﴿And We saved those who believed and used to be mindful of God.﴾

﴿And We saved those who believed and used to be mindful of God.﴾ That is: they feared their Lord and dreaded His threat. And that is by believing in Him alone and affirming His messengers.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 41, verse 19:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[19] ﴿And on the Day when the enemies of Allah are gathered to the Fire, they will be made to stop and be sorted out.﴾

﴿And on the Day when the enemies of Allah are gathered to the Fire, they will be made to stop and be sorted out.﴾ That is: on the Day when they are assembled, for greater disgrace, (p-5195) between the first and the last, the enemies of Allah, the polytheists and the deniers, to the Fire, so that the first of them comes up to the last of them, in order that the proof may be fully established against them all together, and no argument remains for them to make; for they never cease to dispute on behalf of themselves.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[20] ﴿Until, when they reach it, their hearing, their sight, and their skins will testify against them concerning what they used to do.﴾

﴿Until, when they reach it﴾: that is, they exaggerated in denying their disobedience. ﴿Their hearing will testify against them﴾: that is, that they heard the proofs and turned away from them, heard the doubts and followed them, and heard the abominations and considered them good. ﴿And their sight﴾: that is, that they saw the signs and did not take heed of them, and saw the ugly deeds and chose them. ﴿And their skins﴾: that is, that they engaged in the sins, so their effect reached the faculty of touch in them, and thus every organ and every part bears witness. ﴿Concerning what they used to do.﴾

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[21] ﴿And they will say to their skins, "Why did you testify against us?" They will say, "Allah has caused us to speak, He who causes everything to speak. And it is He who created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned."﴾

﴿And they will say to their skins﴾, i.e., those that perceive the pain of the punishment, which hearing and sight do not perceive: ﴿"Why did you testify against us?"﴾, i.e., with that which necessitates their pain. ﴿They will say, "Allah has caused us to speak"﴾, i.e., to this testimony. ﴿"He who causes everything to speak"﴾, i.e., He causes every thing among the animals to speak. This is from the general (ʿāmm) which reason has specified (khaṣṣahu al-ʿaql), like His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah is over all things Competent﴾, i.e., over all things among the things that are within power. This is, while speech is on its apparent meaning and its reality.

It has been said: the intended meaning is the appearance of marks upon the limbs indicating what they were characterized by in the world, through the change of their forms and the like, which Allah inspires in whoever sees them, that this proceeded from them, because of the removal of the veil in the Hereafter. So speech is a metaphor for indication. Al-Qashani said: the meaning of ﴿Their hearing and their sights and their skins will testify against them﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 20] is that the forms of their limbs are changed and their shapes are fashioned in the form of the deeds they committed, and their skins and their hides are altered, so they speak with the tongue of the state and indicate by the forms what they used to do. And by their speaking in this tongue they say: ﴿"Allah has caused us to speak, He who causes everything to speak"﴾, since nothing whatsoever is free of speech, but the heedless do not understand. End.

However, al-Razi said: explaining this testimony as the appearance of specific signs upon these limbs, indicating the issuing of those deeds from them, is a departure from the reality to the metaphor, and the original is its absence.

Then he said: this verse is fitting to cite in explaining that life is not a condition for intelligence, nor for any of the attributes conditioned by life. For Allah, Exalted is He, is Able to create intellect, power, and speech in every part of these limbs. And Allah knows best.

Note:

Al-Razi said: It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: the intended meaning of the testimony of the skins is the testimony of the private parts, and that it is of the category of euphemisms (kināyāt), as He said: ﴿But do not promise them secretly﴾ [al-Baqarah: 235], meaning marriage. And He said: ﴿Or one of you comes from the toilet (al-ghāʾiṭ)﴾ [al-Nisa: 43], meaning relieving oneself. So the verse would be a severe warning concerning fornication. End.

Ibn al-Athir, in (al-Mathal al-Sa'ir), indicated the preference for this meaning, where he mentioned this verse in the discussion of preference between two meanings indicated by one word, which is literal in one and metaphorical in the other. His wording is: "The skins (al-julūd) here is interpreted literally and metaphorically. As for the literal, it means skins in general; as for the metaphorical, it means the private parts specifically. This is the rhetorical factor that favors the metaphorical over the literal, because of the subtle delicacy of the euphemism concerning what is euphemized."

It may be asked here, in weighing between the literal and the metaphorical, about aspects other than the rhetorical one. It is said: What is the explanation of this preference? It is said: the manner of the word "skins" is general, so it is either that it means skins in general, or that it means the limbs which are the instruments of deeds specifically. It is not permissible that it means skins in general, because the testimony of what is not the limbs that are the agents is false testimony, since it is the testimony of one who is not a witness. And testimony here means confession. So the hand says: "I did such and such." And the foot says: "I walked to such and such." Likewise the remaining limbs speak, confessing their deeds. Thus it is preferred by this that the intended meaning is the testimony of the limbs. And if the limbs are intended, it is either that the whole is intended or the part.

If the whole is intended, hearing and sight enter under it, and singling them out by mention would have no benefit. If the part is intended, then it is more specific to the private parts than to the other limbs, for two reasons:

One of them: all the limbs have been mentioned in the Noble Qur'an as testifying against their owner for disobedience except the private parts. So it is more fitting to take "skin" as referring to them, so that the mention of all is completed.

The other: there is among the limbs nothing whose mention is disliked to be explicit except the private parts, so it was alluded to by "skin," because it is a place where it is disliked to explicitly name what it is in its reality.

If it is said: singling out hearing and sight by mention is by way of detailing, like His words: ﴿Fruit and palm trees and pomegranates﴾ [al-Rahman: 68], while palm trees and pomegranates are of the fruit.

I say in reply: this statement is against you, not for you, because the palm tree and the pomegranate were mentioned only to give them distinction in form or in taste, whereas the excellence here in mentioning the testimony is only the magnification of the matter of disobedience. And other than hearing and sight is greater in disobedience, because disobedience of hearing occurs only in listening to backbiting, or to the sound of a flute, or a lute, or what goes in this direction, and disobedience of sight occurs only in looking at what is forbidden; both of these disobediences have no prescribed punishment (ḥadd). As for the sins that occur from other than hearing and sight, they are greater, because disobedience of the hand entails amputation, and disobedience of the private parts entails a hundred lashes or stoning. And this is greater. So it would have been proper to single them out by mention rather than hearing and sight. And when the invalidity of what you have gone to is established, the intended meaning of "skins" is none but the private parts specifically. End of the words of Ibn al-Athir.

Ibn Abi al-Hadid debated him in (al-Falak al-Da'ir) with what its summary amounts to: that carrying "skin" upon the private parts is only specified if there is a relation between the two words "skin" and "private parts," or between their meanings, and we find no relation except that the skin is a part of the constituent reality of the private parts. So the whole is expressed by the part, and that is very far-fetched. End.

I say: the intended purpose of those from whom it is transmitted that the private parts are meant by "skins" is the intention of the most important and most powerful individual. This is because "skins" applies to what the body contains of limbs and muscles that acquire the crime, and it is not hidden that the most important of them in concern and the most deserving of intention is the private parts, because their disobedience outweighs all of them. It is known of the Salaf exegetes that they confine the general to its most important instance in interpretation, as in their restricting "the path of Allah" (sabīl Allāh) to jihad, although "the path of Allah" applies to everything that contains good and nearness to Allah, and benefit and help, and obedience; but the most important of all is fighting those who bar from the truth. So mention of jihad does not negate others. This is a benefit that everyone who has concern for tafsir should strive to understand, for it is among its noble benefits, and by it difficulties not a few are resolved. And Allah is the Granter of success.

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned﴾ are either part of the speech of the skins, or a resumed statement of His own speech, Exalted is He. In either case, it confirms what precedes it: that the One Able to create the first time is Able to make everything speak.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[22] ﴿You did not hide yourselves [from fear] that your hearing would testify against you, nor your sight, nor your skins, but you thought that God does not know much of what you do.﴾

﴿You did not hide yourselves [from fear] that your hearing would testify against you, nor your sight, nor your skins﴾: that is, you did not hide yourselves when committing the indecencies and wrongs, out of defiance or dislike that the aforementioned [limbs] should testify against you. That is, their concealment was not out of fear of what was mentioned, but out of fear of people. Here, ﴿an yashhada﴾ (that it should testify) is an object of purpose (*maf'ul lahu*), with an omitted noun (*mudaf*) understood, or [it is] "from that it should testify," or "against that it should testify." Or it is taken to imply the meaning of *zann* (supposing), so it is in the accusative position. The verse contains a reminder that the believer should be certain that no state passes over him without a watcher over him, as Abu Nuwas said:

Whenever you are alone for a day, do not say, "I was alone," but say, "A watcher is over me."

Do not suppose that God is heedless for an hour, nor that what is hidden from you is absent.

﴿But you thought that God does not know much of what you do﴾: that is, you did not suppose that God knows and therefore makes the limbs speak; rather, you supposed that He does not know much, namely what you do in secret. So you did not conceal yourselves from it and you dared to commit sins. If ﴿an yashhada﴾ is an object of purpose, the meaning is: you did not conceal yourselves by veils, out of fear that the limbs would testify against you; therefore you did not conceal yourselves from them. But [you concealed yourselves] because of your supposition that God does not know much, and therefore you strove to hide from creation, not from the Creator, nor from what the limbs speak of.

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[23] ﴿And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord; it has destroyed you, and you have become among the losers.﴾

﴿And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord; it has destroyed you﴾ — i.e., it caused you to perish through your audacity in opposing Him in the world, and in disputing with Him on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿So you have become among the losers﴾ — i.e., of the deeds of salvation and of the ranks in the Hereafter.

**On the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:**

[24] ﴿Whether they endure patiently, the Fire is their abode; and if they ask to be granted relief, they will not be among those granted relief.﴾

﴿Whether they endure patiently﴾, i.e., over the Fire: ﴿the Fire is their abode﴾, i.e., their dwelling-place and residence. ﴿And if they ask to be granted relief﴾, i.e., they seek al-'utba (ꜥutbā, reconciliation or restoration), which is the return to those whom they loved: ﴿they will not be among those granted relief﴾, i.e., those who are answered in that request, so the punishment will not be lightened for them.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 41, verses 25–26:

(p-5200) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[25, 26] ﴿And We appointed for them companions who made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them, and the word came into effect against them, [as it did] among nations that had passed on before them of jinn and mankind. Indeed, they were losers.﴾ ﴿And those who disbelieved said, "Do not listen to this Qur'an, and speak noisily over it that you may overcome."﴾ [Fussilat: 26].

﴿And We appointed for them companions﴾ means: We sent to them counterparts from the devils who became associated with them. ﴿And they made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them﴾ means: they made their deeds seem good to them, all of them, the present and the future. The two extremes are then a metaphor for the whole. Or, what is before them is the crimes of this world, and what is behind them is the denial of the Return. Al-Shihab said: Explaining the affairs of this world as "what is before them" is because they are present to them, like a thing between your hands that you turn about however you wish; and the Hereafter as "what is behind them" is because it is not witnessed, like a thing behind you; or because it will overtake them. It may also be reversed, so that what is before them is the Hereafter, since it is future, and what is behind them is this world, since it has passed and been left behind, as was mentioned shortly before.

Al-Qashani said in his interpretation of the verse: That is, We ordained for them intimate friends and peers from the devils of mankind or of the jinn, from illusion and imagination, because of their remoteness from the Higher Assembly, and their essential opposition to the holy souls and the angelic lights, through their immersion in hylic matter, and their veiling by the bodily attributes, and their attraction to bodily desires and natural lusts. Thus they were suited to the wretched earthly souls, the turbid and dark ones, and they opposed the holy substances. So the devils were made their companions, and they were veiled from the light of the dominion. ﴿And they made attractive to them what was before them﴾ means: what was in their presence of bestial and predatory pleasures and natural lusts; ﴿and what was behind them﴾ means: of hopes and wishes that they do not attain; ﴿and the word came into effect against them﴾ means: in the divine decree, for everlasting wretchedness; ﴿among nations that had passed on before them﴾ of those who denied their prophets, the astray and the misleading; ﴿of jinn and mankind. Indeed, they were losers.﴾ ﴿And those who disbelieved said﴾ [Fussilat: 26], that is: they concealed the adornment of the Qur'an's proofs from their followers, whom they had made attractive with their feeble doubts: ﴿"Do not listen to this Qur'an"﴾ [Fussilat: 26], that is: when it is recited, and do not incline to it, lest its admonition affect you; ﴿and speak noisily over it﴾ [Fussilat: 26], that is: bring up idle talk during its recitation, so that it becomes confused and he cannot recite. By idle talk is meant that which has no basis, or that which has no meaning; ﴿that you may overcome﴾ [Fussilat: 26], that is: you may turn away whoever wishes to hear it from hearing it, so he does not hear it. And if he does not hear it and does not understand it, he will not follow it. Thus you will overcome with this scheme of yours its proofs, by which it overcomes your minds.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 41, verses 27–28:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[27, 28] ﴿So We will surely make those who disbelieve taste a severe punishment, and We will surely recompense them with the worst of what they used to do. [29] ﴿And those who disbelieve will say, "Our Lord, show us those who misguided us from among the jinn and mankind; we will place them under our feet so that they will be among the lowest.")﴾.

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[30] ﴿Indeed, those who have said, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remained steadfast, the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good news of Paradise, which you were promised."﴾

﴿Indeed, those who have said, "Our Lord is Allah"﴾, i.e., they affirmed His oneness by negating anything other than Him, and they knew Him with certainty, in the truest sense of knowing Him. ﴿Then remained steadfast﴾, i.e., in their character, their beliefs, and their deeds. ﴿Do not fear﴾, i.e., what you are about to face after your death. ﴿And do not grieve﴾, i.e., over what you have left behind of your worldly life, of family and children; for We will take your place in all of that. Al-Qashani said: The angels only descend upon them because of the true affinity between them in true monotheism, certain faith, and deeds firmly established upon the path of truth and uprightness in the way leading to Him, without breaking their resolve, deviating from their direction, or going astray in their actions. His words, exalted is He: ﴿And receive good news of Paradise, which you were promised﴾, i.e., in this world, while still in faith in the Unseen.

[31–32] ﴿We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. Therein you shall have whatever your souls desire, and therein you shall have whatever you ask for.﴾ ﴿An accommodation from One who is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [Fussilat: 32].

﴿We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾ That is: your beloved friends in both abodes, owing to the affinity between us and you. Just as the devils are allies of the disbelievers, because of the kinship between them and the sharing in darkness and turbidity. Ibn Kathir said: That is, the angels say to the believers at the time of death: "We were your companions in the life of this world, guiding you, granting you success, and protecting you by the command of God. Likewise, we will be with you in the Hereafter: we will dispel the loneliness from you in the graves and at the blowing of the Trumpet, we will give you security on the Day of Resurrection and Rising, we will bring you across the Straight Path (al-Sirat), and we will bring you to the Gardens of Bliss."

Al-Razi said: The meaning of their being allies of the believers is that the angels have influences upon human souls, through inspirations and certain unveilings, just as the devils have influences upon souls, by casting whisperings into them and presenting falsehoods to them. In sum, the angels' being allies of the good and pure souls arises from many known aspects, for those who possess unveilings and direct witnessings. Thus they say: Just as that alliance was present in this world, it will remain in the Hereafter, for those bonds are intrinsic, necessary, and not subject to cessation. Rather, after death they become even stronger and more lasting. (p-5205) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[33] ﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah and does righteousness and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims."﴾

﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah and does righteousness and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims."﴾ That is: there is no one better in speech than one who calls people to the worship of Allah, the Exalted, and who is among the righteous who enjoin good, and who submits their faces to Him, the Exalted, in monotheism.

Subtleties:

The first: Al-Qashani said: He placed the calling to the truth and the perfecting of others first, because it is the most noble of ranks, and because it necessitates scholarly and practical perfection; otherwise the calling would not be valid. End.

The second: In the verse there is an indication of encouraging the Prophet (ﷺ) to turn away from the polytheists and from the idle talk they uttered regarding the revelation, which Allah related about them earlier. It also guides him to persevere in conveying and calling (to Islam), by explaining that this is the best of acts of obedience and the foremost of acts of worship. This is the secret of the placement of this verse after what preceded it. There is another aspect: the ranks of felicity are two: complete and more complete. As for the complete, it is that one acquires the virtuous attributes by which one becomes perfect in one's own self. When one finishes this rank, one then occupies oneself with perfecting those who are deficient.

So His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾ [Fussilat: 30] is an indication of the first rank, which is acquiring the states that bring about the perfection of the soul in its essence. When one has finished this rank, it becomes necessary to move to the second rank, which is moving on to perfecting the deficient; and this occurs only through calling creation to the true religion, which is what is meant by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And who is better in speech﴾, the verse...

Know that whoever Allah has granted a strong disposition and a full share of divine sciences recognizes that there is no arrangement better or more perfect than the arrangement of the verses of the Qur'an. (Reported by al-Razi.)

(p-5206) The third: Within the verse enters everyone who calls to Allah by one of the legislated methods and one of the transmitted paths, because the correct calling is the prophetic calling, and then whoever follows its method in proclaiming the truth and preferring it over the creation.

The fourth: In the verse there is evidence for the obligation of calling to Allah, the Exalted, according to what al-Razi established, because calling to Allah is the best of deeds, and whatever is the best of deeds is obligatory.

The fifth: Those who permitted the saying "I am a Muslim" without conditioning it on the will (of Allah) argued with this verse, and said: its unrestricted form indicates that this is the preferable. The matter is well known, and al-Ghazali expounded it in (Ihya').

Imam Ibn Hazm, in (al-Fisal), has a subtle verification that is worth citing. He, may Allah have mercy on him, said: People differed regarding the statement of a Muslim: "I am a believer." It has been transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud and a group of his distinguished companions, and those after them among the jurists, that he disliked this, and used to say: "I am a believer, if Allah wills." Some of them said: "I believe in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers." And they used to say: whoever says "I am a believer," let him say: "Indeed, I am among the people of Paradise."

Then Ibn Hazm said: Our view on this matter is that this is a attribute that a person knows of himself. If he knows that he affirms Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and Muhammad (ﷺ), and everything that he brought, peace be upon him, and that he confesses with his tongue to all of that, then it is obligatory upon him to acknowledge it, as Allah, exalted, commanded when He said: ﴿And as for the favor of your Lord, proclaim it﴾ [al-Duha: 11]. And there is no favor more emphatic, more excellent, or more deserving of thanks than the favor of Islam. So it is obligatory upon him to say: "I am a Muslim with certainty before Allah, the Exalted, and at this moment of mine." There is no difference between his saying "I am a believer, a Muslim" and his saying "I am black" or "I am white."

Likewise all his other attributes about which there is no doubt. This is not a matter of self-praise or boasting in anything, because it is obligatory upon him to protect his blood with the testimony of monotheism. Allah, exalted, said: ﴿Say: We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes, and what was given to Moses and Jesus and what was given to the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we are Muslims﴾ [al-Baqarah: 136]. (p-5207) The saying of Ibn Mas'ud is, in our view, correct, because Islam and faith are two terms transferred from their linguistic meanings to all righteousness and acts of obedience. Ibn Mas'ud only forbade saying "I am a Muslim believer" in the sense that one has fulfilled all acts of obedience, and this is correct. Whoever claims this for himself has lied without doubt. Nothing prevented him, may Allah be pleased with him, from saying that a person may say "I am a believer" in the sense of "one who affirms." How so, when he himself says: "Say: I believe in Allah and His messengers"? That is: I affirmed. As for whoever says, "Say: You are in Paradise," the answer is that we say: if we die in the state we are in now, then we will undoubtedly enter Paradise. The proof of this is that it has been established from the texts of the Qur'an, the Sunnah, and the consensus that whoever believes in Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) and in everything he brought, and does not commit what is disbelief, then he is in Paradise. However, we do not know what will be done to us in this world, and we are not secure from the plotting of Allah, the Exalted, nor from His leading astray, nor from the plotting of Satan, and we do not know what we will earn tomorrow, and we seek refuge in Allah from abandonment. End.

**Commentary on His words, may He be exalted:**

﴿And not equal are the good deed and the evil deed. Repel [evil] with that which is better, and thereupon the one between whom and you there is enmity will be as though he were a devoted friend.﴾

﴿And not equal are the good deed and the evil deed﴾: that is, because the first comes from the station of the intellect (*al-'aql*) and draws its doer to Paradise and to the company of the angels, while the second comes from the station of the self (*al-nafs*) and draws its doer to the Fire and to the company of the devils. ﴿Repel [evil] with that which is better﴾: that is, repel the evil deed wherever it confronts you with that which is better than it, namely the good deed. This is on the basis that what is meant by "the better" is the greater in every respect, or the best of the good deeds with which it can be repelled. He departed from what the apparent wording would require, which is "repel with the good deed," to the more eloquent form, because whoever repels with the better finds it easy to repel with what is lesser than it. This statement is more forceful in urging and exhorting toward what has been mentioned, because it indicates that the matter is one of importance that deserves attention and inquiry.

Al-Qashani said: That is, if you are able to repel the evil of your enemy with the good deed that is better, then do not repel it with a good deed that is lesser. How much less, then, with an evil deed? For evil is not repelled by evil; rather, it increases and rises, as the fire rises by means of firewood. If you meet it with its like, you will have descended to the station of the self, following the devil, treading the path of the Fire, casting your companion into sins, and making him and yourself among the wicked, causing the increase of evil and turning away from good. But if you repel it with the good deed, you extinguish its spark, remove its enmity, remain firm in the station of the heart upon goodness, are guided to Paradise, drive away the devil, please the Most Merciful, enter into the thread of the divine kingdom (*malakut*), and erase your companion's sin through his remorse. Then He, may He be exalted, pointed to the reason for the command and its fruit by His words: ﴿Thereupon the one between whom and you there is enmity will be as though he were a devoted friend﴾: that is, a companion or a close relative, ﴿devoted﴾: that is, of intense loyalty. The origin of *al-hamim* is water of intense heat. He used it as a metaphor for the sincere friend in his affection, because of the heat of love, longing, and concern that he finds in himself toward his beloved.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[35] ﴿And none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune.﴾

﴿And none is granted it⦆ i.e., this noble trait and great virtue, which is repaying evil with good. ﴿except those who are patient⦆ i.e., patient in swallowing hardships, or patient in obedience to Him, Exalted is He, and in His command, adorning themselves with knowledge and forgiveness. ﴿And none is granted it except one of great fortune⦆ i.e., of goodness and perfection of the soul, and from God, Exalted is He, through being characterized by His attributes, and of reward and perfection of intellect.

(p-5209) That is: And if Satan casts into your soul a whisper from the promptings of the self, desiring to move you to repay the wrongdoer with wrongdoing and to take revenge on him, then seek protection in Allah, hold fast against his steps by returning to His presence and taking refuge at His court, from his evil, his whisperings, and his prick.

Ibn Kathir said: We have mentioned that this station has no parallel in the Qur'an except in Surat al-A'raf, where He says: ﴿Take what is pardoned, enjoin what is customary, and turn away from the ignorant﴾ [al-A'raf: 199] ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should prick you, seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ [al-A'raf: 200]. And in Surat al-Mu'minun, where He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Repel evil with that which is better; We are most knowing of what they describe﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 96] ﴿And say: My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the suggestions of the devils﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 97] ﴿And I seek refuge in You, my Lord, lest they be present with me﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 98].

Discourse on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[37] ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day, and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to God who created them, if it is Him that you worship.﴾

﴿And among His signs﴾ i.e., His proofs upon His creation, and His indication of His oneness and the greatness of His dominion.

﴿the night and the day﴾ i.e., their alternation, and each of them succeeding the other. ﴿And the sun and the moon﴾ i.e., their light and their shining, the determination of their stations, and the variation of their courses in their heavens, for the preservation of the good order of the cosmos. ﴿Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon﴾ because they are subjected by the subjugation of a Creator who is able over them; thus they are created beings. ﴿But prostrate to God who created them, if it is Him that you worship﴾ i.e., that you single Him out for worship; for it is among obedience to Him that you devote worship sincerely to Him and do not associate anyone in His obedience, since it is not befitting for anyone other than Him.

Note of caution:

Shaykh Abu Ishaq used the verse as evidence in (al-Muhadhdhab) for the eclipse prayer (salat al-kusuf). He said: because there is no prayer connected with the sun and the moon other than it. And from this it is derived that it is preferred over the prayer for rain (salat al-istisqa'), because it is mentioned in the Qur'an, unlike it. Thus it is in (al-Iklil).

﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth humbled﴾ meaning: still, with no movement of herbage in it, no plant, and no crop. ﴿But when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells﴾ meaning: it stirs with vegetation and moves with its adornment, and it swells by its rising above its surface, that is, it becomes a high mound. ﴿Indeed, He who revived it﴾ meaning: this earth that had become desolate, so He brought forth vegetation from it and made it stir with crops after its dryness. ﴿Is surely the Reviver of the dead. Indeed, He is over all things Competent.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our signs﴾ [Fussilat: 40] meaning: they incline away from Our proofs and evidences, and swerve from them, denying and rejecting them. ﴿Are not hidden from Us﴾ [Fussilat: 40] meaning: because His knowledge encompasses them, and He is watchful over them, so He will recompense them.

Admonition:

The verse includes, in a few words, a discussion of the signs placed out of their proper positions, as Ibn 'Abbas interpreted it. In (al-Iklil) he said: "In it is a refutation of those who undertake the interpretation of the Qur'an with what the essence of the wording does not indicate, as the Batiniyya (esotericists), the Ittihadiyya (monists), the atheists, and the extreme Sufis do." ﴿Is one who is thrown into the Fire better, or one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection? Do what you will; indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.﴾ [Fussilat: 40] ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder﴾ [Fussilat: 41] meaning: this Qur'an ﴿when it has come to them﴾ [Fussilat: 41] meaning: they are then destined for ruin. The predicate is omitted, or the clause is a substitute for the clause ﴿Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our signs﴾ [Fussilat: 40]. ﴿And indeed, it is a Book of might﴾ [Fussilat: 41] meaning: a protected source, safeguarded from alteration and change, and from being imitated with an equal.

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[42] ﴿No falsehood comes to it from before it or from behind it. It is a revelation from One who is All-Wise, Praiseworthy.﴾

﴿No falsehood comes to it from before it or from behind it﴾ means: falsehood cannot find any way to it from any of the directions.

Al-Qashani said: Not from the direction of the Truth, so that He would nullify it with something more eloquent than it and more firmly established in being true and genuine. And not from the direction of the creation, so that they could nullify it by heretical interpretation or alter it by distortion, since it is fixed in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh), guarded from the side of the Truth, as He said: ﴿Indeed, We sent down the Reminder, and indeed We will be its guardian﴾ [al-Hijr: 9]. In this there is an illustration, likening it to a person who is protected from all his sides, so that his enemies cannot reach him, for he is in a secure fortress under the protection of the Manifest Truth. This is on the basis that "what is before it and what is behind it" is a metaphor (kinayah) for all directions, just as "the morning and the evening" is a metaphor for all time. Or the meaning is: no falsehood can reach it in any of the reports it gives, past or future. "What is before it" is the past, and "what is behind it" is the future. Or the reverse, as has passed.

﴿A revelation from One who is All-Wise, Praiseworthy﴾. Ibn Jarir said: That is, it is a revelation from One who possesses wisdom, in managing His servants and directing them toward what holds their welfare, and who is praised for His blessings upon them through His favours that they possess.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 41, verse 43:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[43] ﴿Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you. Indeed, your Lord is the possessor of forgiveness and the possessor of painful punishment.﴾

﴿Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you﴾ means: what your people among the disbelievers say to you is only like what the disbelievers among the people of the messengers said to them, of harmful words and slander against the revealed Books. That is, be patient as they were patient. ﴿Indeed, your Lord is the possessor of forgiveness﴾ means: for the sins of those who turn back to Him in repentance from their sins, by pardoning them. ﴿And the possessor of painful punishment﴾ means: for those who persist in their disbelief and their sins and die without repenting of them.

The commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 41, verse 44:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[44] ﴿And if We had made it a non-Arabic Qur'an, they would have said, "Why are its verses not explained in detail? Is it a non-Arabic recitation and an Arab [messenger]?" Say, "It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing. And those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is blindness for them. Those are being called from a distant place."﴾

﴿And if We had made it a non-Arabic Qur'an, they would have said, "Why are its verses not explained in detail?"﴾ That is: its proofs and its contents are made clear, in a tongue we recognize, so that we may understand what is in it. Al-Zamakhshari said: Out of their obstinacy, they used to say, "Why was the Qur'an not sent down in the language of the non-Arabs?" It was said in reply: even if it were as they propose, they would not abandon objection and obstinacy, and they would say, "Why are its verses not explained in detail and summarized in a tongue we understand?" ﴿Is it non-Arabic and Arab?﴾ The hamza here is the hamzat al-inkar (the interrogative of denial), meaning: they would deny it and say, "A non-Arabic Qur'an and an Arab messenger?" Or, "A non-Arabic [recitation] and an Arab addressed by it?" The meaning is that the signs of God, in whatever manner they came to them, they would deny, being obstinate; because these people are not seeking the truth, but merely follow their desires. End of quotation.

Al-Shihab said: al-a'jami (non-Arabic) is originally (a'jam), and its meaning is one whose speech is not understood because of a speech impediment, or because of the strangeness of his language; the ya' is added for emphasis, as in ahmari (very red). It is applied to his speech figuratively, but it has become so well known that it is treated as a literal usage. As for al-'ajami, it refers to what is ascribed to the 'ajam (non-Arabs), who are all those other than the Arabs, and it is sometimes restricted to the people of Persia and to their language, also called al-'ajamiyya. Thus between al-a'jami and al-'ajami there is a partial overlap of general and specific meaning. End of quotation.

﴿Say, "It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing."﴾ That is: it is for the believers in the unseen, a guidance that leads them to the truth, and enlightens them with knowledge, and a healing that removes the diseases of their hearts from vices such as hypocrisy and doubt. That is, it enlightens them about the way of reflection and action, so it teaches them and purifies them. ﴿And those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is blindness for them.﴾ That is: they neither hear it nor understand it. Rather, it is confused for them, because heedlessness has taken hold of them and the natural veils have blocked the channels of their hearts' hearing and sight, so that it does not penetrate them, and they neither take heed nor awaken. ﴿Those are being called from a distant place.﴾ That is: their condition in not accepting the truth and not listening to it is like that of one who is called from a very far distance, from which the voice cannot be heard, so the call is not heard. This is because of their distance from the source of light by which the truth is perceived and seen, and their immersion in the darkness of matter.

Al-Shihab said: He made the calling from a distant place an image of their not understanding and not benefiting from what they were called to. It is said: "You are being called from a distant place," meaning: you do not understand what I say. It was also said: it is literal, and that on the Day of Resurrection they will be called in this way, as a disgrace to them.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 41, verse 45:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[45] ﴿And We gave Moses the Book, but differences arose concerning it. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been decided between them. And indeed they are in disquieting doubt concerning it.﴾

﴿And We gave Moses the Book, but differences arose concerning it﴾. Ibn Jarir said: that is, they differed in acting upon what it contains, those among the Jews who were given it. Ibn Kathir said: that is, he was denied and harmed. ﴿So be patient, as the messengers of determination were patient﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 35]. ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾, and it is the promise of the Resurrection and the decisive judgment of the dispute at that time; that is, had it not been that Allah, exalted is He, ordained the recompense for the Hereafter: ﴿it would have been decided between them﴾, that is, by hastening the punishment: ﴿Nay, for them is an appointed time from which they will find no refuge other than it﴾ [al-Kahf: 58]. ﴿Nay, the Hour is their appointed time, and the Hour is more calamitous and more bitter﴾ [al-Qamar: 46]. ﴿And indeed they are in disquieting doubt concerning it﴾, that is, one that causes unease and agitation for themselves and their followers, due to the blindness of their insight and the dullness of their minds; otherwise the truth is too clear to be hidden. Ibn Kathir said: that is, their denial of it was not out of insight on their part when they spoke; rather they were doubting what they said, not certain of anything they were in. This is how Ibn Jarir directed it, and it is possible. And Allah knows best.

Commentary on His words, exalted is He:

[46] ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul; and whoever does evil, it is against it. And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants.﴾

﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 15] — that is: whoever acts in obedience to Allah, complying with His command and refraining from what He has forbidden, the benefit of it accrues to his own soul, because he will be recompensed for it with its good reward. ﴿And whoever does evil﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 15] — that is: whoever commits an evil deed and disobeys, ﴿it is against it﴾, its harm falls upon him, because he has inflicted injury upon his own soul thereby, for it has earned for it the wrath of Allah, exalted is He, and the painful punishment. And: ﴿And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ — that is: He does not punish anyone except for his own sin, and He does not chastise anyone except after the establishment of the proof against him and the sending of a Messenger to him.

(p-٥٢١٥)﴿To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour.﴾ That is: none knows it but Him. Or the meaning is: if He is asked about it, it is said, "Allah is the Knower of it." ﴿And no fruit emerges from its coverings﴾ — that is, its sheaths (*awa'iyatiha*). ﴿Nor does any female conceive or give birth except with His knowledge﴾ — that is, accompanied by His knowledge. Al-Zamakhshari said: He knows the number of the days and hours of the pregnancy, and its conditions: whether it ends in miscarriage (*al-khidaj*) or is complete, whether the child is male or female, beautiful or ugly, and other matters. ﴿And [mention] the Day He will call to them, "Where are My partners?"﴾ — that is, those whom you associated with Me in worship. ﴿They will say, "We announce to You that none of us is a witness."﴾ That is: we inform You that none of us now bears witness to their partnership or acknowledges it. As for {شَهِيدٌ} (*shahid*, "witness"), it is on the pattern *fa'il* derived from *al-shahada* (testimony). The negation of testimony is a metaphor for disavowing them. Or it may be that their saying "none of us is a witness" is a denial of their worship of them, and so it would be a lie, like their saying: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23].

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[48] ﴿And what they used to call upon before has strayed from them, and they will think that they have no place of escape.﴾

﴿And what they used to call upon before has strayed from them﴾ — i.e., what they used to worship of idols, so they neither benefited them nor warded off anything from them. ﴿And they will think that they have no place of escape﴾ — i.e., they will be certain on that Day that they have no refuge to which they can flee from the punishment of Allah.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[49] ﴿Man does not tire of asking for good, but if evil touches him, he is despairing and hopeless.﴾

﴿Man does not tire of asking for good﴾ — that is, he does not grow weary of asking his Lord for good things, such as wealth and health of body. ﴿But if evil touches him﴾ — that is, harm befalls him in himself, through sickness, or hardship in his livelihood. ﴿He is despairing and hopeless﴾ — that is, despairing of the mercy and compassion of Allah, and of His removing what has befallen him. Al-Zamakhshari (al-Zamakhshari) said: it is intensified in two ways: through the pattern (fa'ul) and through repetition. And qunut (qunut, hopelessness) is that the trace of despair appears upon him, so that he shrinks and is broken.

(p-5216) The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[50] ﴿And if We let him taste mercy from Us after some hardship had touched him, he will surely say, "This is mine, and I do not think the Hour will ever come. And even if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely have the best with Him." But We will inform those who disbelieved of what they did, and We will surely make them taste a severe punishment.﴾

﴿And if We let him taste mercy from Us after some hardship had touched him﴾ i.e., by relieving it from him. ﴿He will surely say, "This is mine"﴾ i.e., it is my due; I have attained it by my own deeds, not by a bounty from Allah, denying the One who bestowed the favor. ﴿And I do not think the Hour will ever come. And even if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely have the best with Him﴾ i.e., the best state of honor, out of greed and guessing at the unseen, and playing with whatever desire dictates. ﴿But We will inform those who disbelieved of what they did﴾ i.e., We will surely inform these people who wish vain things about Allah of the reality of their deeds, and We will show them the opposite of what they believed about them. ﴿And We will surely make them taste a severe punishment﴾, which is their being abiding in the Fire.

The discussion of His saying, the Exalted:

[51] ﴿And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself (lit. turns away with his side); but when evil touches him, he is one of lengthy supplication.﴾

﴿And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself⁠⁠ ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠(with his side)﴾ meaning: when We remove from him the harm he has, and grant him wealth, health, and ease, he turns away from the obedience to which he was called, and becomes arrogant, lifting his nose high, refusing to respond. ﴿But when evil touches him, he is one of abundant supplication﴾ meaning: he is one of much supplication, who persists in his humble pleading and spends his breaths absorbed in earnest entreaty. The word (al-ʿarḍ, "breadth") has been borrowed (istiʿāra) for the abundance of supplication, just as (al-ṭūl, "length") is also borrowed for it. It is said: "So-and-so lengthened his supplication" (aṭāla fulān al-duʿāʾ), when he made it abundant; and likewise "he broadened his supplication" (aʿraḍa duʿāʾahu).

(p-٥٢١٧)The discourse on the interpretation (*ta'wil*, the explanation of a verse's meaning) of His saying:

[52] ﴿Say: "Have you considered: if it is from Allah, and you then disbelieve in it, who is more astray than one who is in extreme opposition?"﴾

﴿Say: Have you considered if﴾ i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿is from Allah, and you then disbelieve in it﴾ i.e., without reflection and without following evidence, ﴿who is more astray than one who is in extreme opposition﴾ i.e., who is more astray than you? He placed the relative noun (*al-mawsul*) in the place of the relative clause (*al-silah*), to explain their condition and to give the reason for their increased straying. *Al-shiqaq* is opposition, because the one who opposes is on one side and in one direction, apart from the one he opposes.

Al-Shihab (al-Alusi) said: The verse is a return to confronting the critics and the deniers, and He concluded the surah with what turns back to the beginning of the surah. It is of fair speech, and in it is an urging to reflection and a gentle leading toward acknowledgment, along with the magic of eloquence it contains. The mention of the Hour came in between as a completion of the warning and an alert to the far-reaching error they are in.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[53] ﴿We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves, until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. Is it not sufficient that your Lord is, over all things, a Witness?﴾

﴿We shall show them Our signs in the horizons﴾ meaning: the campaigns of the Prophet (ﷺ) in the regions of the land of the polytheists, from the people of Makkah and its surroundings, and his dominance over the people, as confirmation of the promise. ﴿And within themselves﴾, i.e., from their defeat, subjugation, and the breaking of their power, as happened at Badr and the Conquest of Makkah. ﴿Until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth﴾, i.e., that this Qur'an, with its promise and its warning, is the established truth; for there is no proof after direct witnessing. God has given victory to His Messenger and his companions, and abandoned falsehood and its party. ﴿Is it not sufficient that your Lord is, over all things, a Witness?﴾, i.e., nothing whatsoever is hidden from Him of what His creation does, and He will recompense them for it; so in this is both a promise and a warning.

(p-5218) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[54] ﴿Certainly, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord. Certainly, He is encompassing of all things.﴾

﴿Certainly, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord﴾ i.e., in great doubt about the resurrection after death and their return to their Lord. ﴿Certainly, He is encompassing of all things﴾ i.e., nothing escapes His encompassing. ﴿Does not He know who created? And He is the Subtle, the Acquainted [with all things].﴾ [al-Mulk: 14]
